transcript.text: Water started coming into my basement last night after the storm. I don't know who to call.

I'm sorry, that's stressful. A water damage restoration company is the right first call. They'll pump out the water and dry things out so mold doesn't set in.

Safety first: if the water is anywhere near outlets, cords, appliances or your electrical panel, stay out of the basement. Don't step in the water. If you can reach the panel without standing in water, switch off the breaker for the basement. If you can't, call your electric utility.

Two quick questions so I can find someone nearby:
1. What's your ZIP code?
2. Roughly how much water is down there (damp spots, an inch or two, or deeper), and is more still coming in?
It's 94087. There's about 2 inches across the floor, coming in along the back wall, and yeah it still seems to be seeping in a bit.

Two inches with water still coming in counts as an emergency, so I looked for companies that can come out right away. Here are the best matches near Sunnyvale:

1. Clearway Restoration, +1-408-457-0826. Closest at about 5.8 km in Santa Clara, and they advertise 24/7 emergency service. This is my top pick.
2. Reactic Restoration, +1-408-998-4840. Also 24/7, but farther away at about 11.4 km in San Jose.
3. Servpro, +1 650-770-2992. In Sunnyvale about 6.6 km away. It doesn't list 24/7 hours, so it's better as a backup.

I can send your request to Clearway now so they call you back, and I'd list the other two as backups. If that works, please send:
- Your full name and best phone number (plus email if you'd like)
- The service address with city, state and ZIP
- When someone can come (I'm guessing as soon as possible?)
- Whether you own or rent, and the type of home (house, townhouse, condo...)
- Whether you plan to file an insurance claim, and with whom, if you know

While you wait, move valuables and boxes off the floor, and take photos of the water and damage for your insurer.

Yes, please send it to Clearway. I'm Maria Lopez, 408-555-0142, maria.lopez@example.com, and the address is 1032 Hollenbeck Ave, Sunnyvale CA 94087. I own it, it's a single family house, and I'm home all day so ASAP works; I'll probably file with State Farm.

Thanks, Maria. I have everything I need. One quick check before I send it: is it OK to share your name, phone, email and address with Clearway Restoration? If they can't take the job, I'd also pass it to Reactic Restoration and Servpro as backups.

And would you rather they call or text you?
Yes, that's fine, share it with all three if needed. A call is better, I'll keep my phone on me.

Your request is in, Maria. Lead ID: LEAD-20261008-5AE690.

- It's ready to go to Clearway Restoration, +1-408-457-0826, marked as an emergency, and asks them to call you back.
- If they can't take it, Reactic Restoration and Servpro are lined up as backups.

Since water is still coming in, I'd also call Clearway yourself right now. Give them the lead ID so they can pull up your details. They should come out, pump the water, find where it's getting in, and set up drying equipment.

While you wait:
- Stay out of the water unless the basement power is off.
- Take photos and video of the water and anything damaged.
- Call State Farm to start your claim, and tell Clearway it's an insurance job.

I hope they get it dried out quickly.
my furnace stopped working and the house is getting really cold

I'm sorry, a cold house is miserable. Let's get someone out to you.

One safety point first: if you smell gas (a rotten-egg smell) near the furnace, leave the house now and call your gas utility or 911 from outside.

A couple of quick questions:
1. What's your ZIP code (or city and state)?
2. What's the furnace doing? Is it completely dead, is the fan running but blowing cold air, or is there an error light? And roughly how cold is it inside now?
no gas smell. 94087, sunnyvale. fan runs but its blowing cold air, its 57 in here and thermostat is set to 70

57°F is too cold to wait on, so I treated this as urgent. A fan that runs but blows cold air usually means the burner isn't lighting. That's often an ignitor, flame sensor or safety switch problem, and it's a common repair.

While you wait, a few safe checks:
- Make sure the thermostat is set to HEAT (not COOL or OFF) and the fan is on AUTO, not ON.
- If the furnace filter looks very dirty, replace it. A clogged filter can make the furnace shut its burner off for safety.

Here's who I found near 94087:

2. ProTemp Mechanical Incorporated in Santa Clara is closer (5.4 km), but the listing has no phone number, only their website (protemp.net).

Until then, keep your little one in one warm room with the door closed and add layers. If you use a space heater, keep it at least 3 feet from bedding, curtains and little hands, and don't leave it running overnight.
One of the outlets in my kitchen sparked and now half the kitchen has no power.

That sounds scary. I'm glad you're okay. Here's what to do first:

- Don't use or touch that outlet, and unplug anything that was plugged into it if you can do it safely.
- If you smell burning, see smoke, or the outlet or wall plate feels warm or looks scorched, turn off the breaker for the kitchen at your panel (or the main breaker if you're not sure which one). Only do this if the panel area is dry.
- If you see smoke or flames, get everyone out and call 911.
- For now, don't reset the tripped breaker over and over. If it sparked, there could be a damaged wire or connection behind the outlet.

I'll find a licensed electrician near you. Two quick questions:
1. What's your ZIP code?
2. Do you smell burning or see scorch marks on the outlet, or did it just spark once and then lose power?

I'm in 94087. It sparked once with a pop yesterday evening and the breaker tripped; I tried resetting it but it won't stay on, and there's no burning smell now. I haven't looked closely for scorch marks yet. Should I check, or just leave it alone?

Good that there's no burning smell. A breaker that won't stay on usually means there's a real fault on that circuit, like a short or a burned connection behind the outlet. So the breaker is doing its job.

About checking: you can take a quick look, but don't touch anything. Leave that breaker off, use a flashlight, and look for black or brown marks, melted plastic, or cracks on the outlet and cover plate. Don't take the cover off or poke at it. Whatever you see, the next step is the same: keep the breaker off, stop trying to reset it, and have an electrician find the fault. If you do see scorch marks, mention it so I can pass it along. Use extension cords from working outlets for now, but not for big appliances like a microwave or kettle.

Here are electricians near Sunnyvale:

1. WCI Electric, 408-242-2069, Santa Clara (4.9 km). Listed hours are Mon–Fri 8am–5pm, and you can also reach them by email, so they're easy to contact during business hours.
2. Flores Electric, 408-899-8450, Santa Clara (4.3 km). This is the closest option.
3. University Electric, 408 496 0500, Santa Clara (7.3 km). This is a good backup.

I'd pick WCI Electric first, with Flores Electric as a backup. I can send your request to them so they call you back. If you'd like that, please send:

- Your full name and best phone number (and email if you'd like)
- The service address
- When someone can come, whether you own or rent, and the type of home (house, condo, etc.)

Okay, I'll take a look with a flashlight but won't touch it. Before I send everything, why do you need to know whether I own or rent? I'm Priya Raman, 408-555-0163, and weekday afternoons this week work best for me.

Fair question. Electricians ask because it changes who can approve the work and who usually pays. If you rent, your landlord typically has to authorize electrical repairs and often covers the cost, so the electrician may need to coordinate with them. If you own, you can approve it yourself. It's optional, though. You can skip it and the electrician can ask when they call.

Thanks, Priya. I've noted your name, your phone number (408-555-0163), and that weekday afternoons this week work best. To send the request, I just need:

1. The service street address (I'll assume Sunnyvale, CA 94087 unless you tell me otherwise)
2. Whether it's a house, condo, apartment, or townhouse, and whether you own or rent, if you're comfortable sharing

Also, are you okay with me sharing your name, phone number, and address with WCI Electric, with Flores Electric as a backup, so they can call you back? And if you spot any scorch marks with the flashlight, let me know and I'll add that to the request.

That makes sense, thanks. It's 820 E Fremont Ave Unit 12, Sunnyvale 94087. It's a townhouse and I own it, and yes, you can share my info with WCI Electric, and Flores as a backup. My email is priya.r@example.com if that helps.

Your request is set up. The reference number is LEAD-20261008-B5FF1A.

- It's going to WCI Electric, 408-242-2069 (wcielectric.com), with Flores Electric (408-899-8450) as the backup.
- I included everything you told me: the outlet sparked with a pop yesterday, the breaker won't stay on, about half the kitchen has no power, there's no burning smell now, and weekday afternoons work for you.

What to expect next: WCI should call you at 408-555-0163 to set up a time. Their listed hours are Mon–Fri 8am–5pm. If you'd like to move faster, or haven't heard from them by tomorrow afternoon, call them yourself and mention the reference number. If they can't fit you in, call Flores.

Until then, keep that breaker off and don't reset it again. If you spot scorch marks with the flashlight, tell the electrician when they call. And if you ever smell burning or see smoke, get out and call 911.
Hi, there's a brown stain spreading on my ceiling, I think the roof is leaking

Sorry you're dealing with that. A spreading stain usually means water is still getting in, so it's good to catch it now.

A quick safety note: if the stain is near a light fixture or ceiling fan, or the ceiling is sagging, switch that circuit off at the breaker and keep people out from under it. Put a bucket down if it's dripping.

Two quick questions so I can find the right roofer:
1. What's your ZIP code?
2. Is it actively dripping right now, or just a stain that's getting bigger (for example, after rain)?
ZIP is 94087, I'm in Sunnyvale. It's not dripping right now, it only drips when we get heavy rain, and the stain's about the size of a dinner plate in my hallway.

Thanks. That sounds like a leak that only lets water in during heavy rain, so it isn't an emergency. It's still worth getting it fixed before the next storm. Here are the closest roofers I found near 94087:

how much does it cost to fix a water heater

It depends a lot on what's wrong and what kind of heater you have. Rough US ranges, including labor:

- Common repairs (heating element, thermostat, thermocouple, pilot or igniter, anode rod): about $150-$500
- Bigger repairs (gas control valve, or a leaking valve or fitting): about $300-$800
- A leaking tank usually can't be fixed and has to be replaced. A standard tank installed runs about $1,200-$3,500, and tankless about $3,000-$6,000+.

Most plumbers also charge a service call fee of about $75-$200, which is sometimes credited toward the repair.

If you tell me two things, I can narrow that down and find plumbers near you:
1. What's going on? For example no hot water, not enough hot water, leaking, or strange noises. And is it gas or electric, tank or tankless?
2. What's your ZIP code?

If water is actively leaking, turn off the cold water valve above the heater and cut the power (breaker) or set the gas to "pilot" or "off." If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility or 911 from outside.

It's gas, a 40 gallon tank in the garage, and it's about 12 years old. Water's only been lukewarm since Sunday and there's a small puddle under it. ZIP is 94087. Does a puddle mean I'm looking at the expensive replacement?

Not always, but with your setup it's likely.

A puddle can come from cheap parts. The relief valve on the side, the drain valve at the bottom, or a loose fitting on the pipes up top can all leak, and each is usually a $150-$400 fix. But your tank is 12 years old (most last 8-12), the water has gone lukewarm, and it's leaking. Together those usually mean sediment buildup and a failing tank. If water is coming out of the tank itself, like the bottom seam or under the jacket, it has to be replaced. In the Bay Area, a 40-gallon gas tank installed with permit and earthquake straps often runs about $2,000-$3,500.

A quick check: wipe the area dry and see where the water comes back first. Valve or pipe means a possible repair. Bottom of the tank means replacement. If the puddle is growing, turn off the cold water valve above the heater and set the gas control to "pilot" or "off."

I honestly don't know their pricing policy. My listing doesn't show whether they charge a trip fee or quote upfront. You don't need to give me anything to find out, though. You can call them first at +1-650-856-3400 and ask:

- Do you charge a service call or diagnostic fee? If I go ahead with the work, is it credited toward the job?
- Can you give a ballpark over the phone for replacing a 40-gallon gas tank, including permit, haul-away and earthquake straps?
- Will I get a written, itemized quote before any work starts?

Most reputable plumbers will give a rough replacement range over the phone, since it's a common job. They'll still want to look before giving a firm price, to check venting, gas line, and code updates.

You also don't have to agree to anything on the visit. Ask for the itemized quote, and if the number seems high, pay only the diagnostic fee (if they charge one) and get a second quote. South Bay Builders (+1-408-892-2562) works as a comparison.

If you'd rather I send the request, I can add a note saying you want the diagnostic fee confirmed before the visit and an itemized written quote before any work. Just tell me if you want that, or if you'd rather call them yourself.
